validity_findings: Substrate substitution (prereg section 2 named Flask; stdlib http.server used instead): Disclosed in validity_notes, self-test verified ETag/304, session-scoped bodies, 401/403, CRUD behaviour before any arm ran. No evidence this substitution affected the mechanism-level measurements.

Cost dynamic range limitation: On this substrate, cold exploration (B-COLD) already achieves 1.0 HTTP request per task for crud-read and query families because the first generic REST candidate (GET /{collection}/{id} and GET /{collection}?q={q}&limit={limit}) matches the substrate's API exactly. This makes the amortized cost ratio target (≤0.85) unreachable for ANY system on read/query families, including a perfect one. This is a validity threat to the ECONOMIC conclusion (D5, D6 cost half) but not to the MECHANISM capability conclusion (D1-D4, D7).

Positive control cost criterion (D6 cost_ratio ≤ 0.50 vs B-COLD) is not discriminating on this substrate: B-COLD also costs 1.0 request per task on the positive control task set (held-out resource-A identifiers), so no system can achieve ≤0.50. The producer correctly identifies this in validity_notes. The positive control's substantive halves (mechanism_success_rate=1.0, binding_accuracy=1.0) pass cleanly.

Single confidence value for treatment: All 150 treatment resolutions emit confidence=0.956522, so treatment ECE is a single-bin quantity (bin [0.9, 1.0], n=150, gap=0.0435). The pooled all-arm ECE (0.0198, n=550, two bins) is the more informative calibration number and is reported alongside. This is disclosed in validity_notes.

Out-of-support generalization: The collection slot was only ever observed holding {items, tags} during induction. Binding it to products (a third, unobserved value) is extrapolation, not interpolation. Disclosed in validity_notes.

Low n for family-stratified inference: 50 tasks per family yields degenerate bootstrap CIs [1.0, 1.0]. No population-level generalization beyond these task constructions is claimed. Disclosed in validity_notes.

Harness-level measurement, not end-to-end agent evaluation: No model, browser, network egress, or external dataset was used. This measures the kernel's inheritance path in a controlled harness. Disclosed in validity_notes.

Three product defects found and fixed during execution (string-only slot alignment, credential leak on constant path, volatile session metadata promoted to precondition). Each is covered by a unit test. These are product behaviour changes inside the lane's authorized code root (src/, tests/) and are part of what was measured. Disclosed in validity_notes.
baseline_findings: B-COLD (cold exploration) is a STRONG baseline, not a strawman: Its fixed generic REST candidate policy happens to match the substrate's API on the first try for read (GET /{collection}/{id}) and query (GET /{collection}?q={q}&limit={limit}), yielding 1.0 HTTP request per task. For write, it takes 1.64 requests on average (candidates: POST /{collection}, PUT /{collection}/{id}, DELETE /{collection}/{id}, ...). This is a substrate artifact, not a baseline weakness.

The three preregistered baselines (B-COLD, B-LITERAL-REPLAY, B-RETRIEVAL-K5) all have mechanism_success_rate=0.0 and end_to_end_success_rate=1.0 (achieved entirely via cold fallback). B-COLD is correctly selected as the best baseline at matched correctness (end_to_end_success ≥ 0.80 in all families, within 0.05 tolerance of treatment's end_to_end_success).

Baseline competence floor (0.80) and matched correctness tolerance (0.05) are correctly applied and make the D5 test HARDER for the treatment, never easier. B-COLD-DOC (documented executor) fails competence floor on crud-write and crud-read (0.0 end-to-end success) and is correctly excluded from D5 denominator. B-LITERAL-REPLAY-FORCED and B-RETRIEVAL-K5-SLOT are diagnostics, not preregistered baselines, correctly excluded.

Null control (NC-SHUFFLED-INTENT) passes: mechanism_success_rate=0.0, abstention_precision=1.0, cost_ratio_vs_B-COLD=1.0. Confirms transfer requires genuine intent structure, not spurious pattern matching.

Incumbent reference curve matches prereg expectation exactly: shipped kernel has no distill_parameterized, distill confidence=0.5 < min_confidence=0.8, resolves same-intent to EXPLORE, paraphrased intent to UNKNOWN, 0% EXECUTABLE on resource-B with 0 HTTP requests. Quantifies the 'SPIDER doesn't work' baseline as intended.

incumbent_same_intent_resolution.reason: candidate exists but confidence is below execution threshold

claim_ceiling: C-PARAM-INHERIT mechanism capability ESTABLISHED in this setting: kernel-integrated distill_parameterized induces transferable mechanisms that correctly bind to never-observed resource-B identifiers (disjoint value sets) with success_rate=1.0, binding_accuracy=1.0, abstention_precision=1.0, false_accept_rate=0.0, ECE=0.043 across 150 transfer tasks (50 per family, 3 families). The economic case (amortized_cost_ratio ≤ 0.85 vs best baseline at matched correctness) is NOT established on this substrate because the cold baseline already operates at the per-task optimum (1.0 HTTP request) for crud-read and query families, leaving no per-task saving to amortize the 100-request induction bill. The positive control cost criterion (≤0.50 vs B-COLD) is similarly non-discriminating on this substrate. The falsification is BOUNDED to this substrate's economics; a substrate with genuine discovery cost (e.g., multi-step auth, pagination, schema discovery) would be needed to separate intrinsic economic failure from substrate artifact. The mechanism itself works and meets all correctness/safety thresholds.
unresolved: Whether the economic failure is intrinsic to parameter inheritance or an artifact of this substrate's low cold-baseline cost is not settled here. Measured break-even is 254 transfer tasks on crud-write and unreachable on crud-read and query; a substrate with genuine discovery cost (multi-step flows, pagination, schema drift) would be needed to separate the two.

The D6 positive control cost criterion (≤0.50 vs B-COLD) is not discriminating on this substrate and no substitute was substituted for it. A follow-up needs either a substrate with real discovery cost or a prereg that treats the cost half of the positive control as expected-to-fail.

Parameter inheritance beyond one collection dimension is untested: the induced slots cover collection, id, q, limit and auth_token only. Whether the same machinery spans schemas with different field names, nested bodies, or multi-step flows is unknown.

Whether the mechanism abstains correctly when a slot is bound outside the observed support is untested in the failure direction; this run only shows that it does not abstain and does succeed on a third collection value (products).

Repair on binding or execution failure (C-DELTA-REPAIR) was explicitly out of scope and remains unmeasured. The fallback path used here is harness-level cold exploration, not a kernel repair capability.

Staleness and freshness (C-FRESHNESS) were not exercised. The mechanism records evidence-scope metadata including observed_distinct_identifiers=2 for the list intent, which reflects the repeated list actions rather than a freshness assessment.
Cross-site transfer (C-CROSSSITE), LLM distillation (C-LLM-INHERIT), and real-browser economics (C-PRODUCT-ECON) remain out of scope and unmeasured.
